aboutH2: Canadian Centre for Addictions: Residential Rehab in Cobourg
intro: The Canadian Centre for Addictions is a premier residential treatment facility located in Ontario, Canada. We specialize in drug rehab and are dedicated to helping individuals overcome alcohol and drug addiction. Our luxury rehab in Cobourg offers a client-centred approach, where our skilled team of addiction counsellors and therapists collaborates with each client to create a personalized recovery program tailored to their unique needs. We provide comprehensive care, from detoxification to aftercare planning, ensuring our residents receive continuous support. Our commitment to 5-star care means that we not only help our residents achieve sobriety but also teach them how to maintain a high-quality, fulfilling life year after year.

pillars.title: Woodlawn Inn, a Short Walk from Cobourg Beach
pillars.body: CCFA's Cobourg residence is Woodlawn Inn, a former hotel at 420 Division Street in the town's Historic District. The waterfront and Cobourg beach are a few minutes away on foot, and the grounds have walking trails and meditation gardens. Most rooms come with a fireplace, a jacuzzi tub, a private deck and a view of the lake. There's a gym and a steam room in the building, massage therapy through the spa, and a chef who cooks every day. The centre also runs a second residence, Hillcrest Mansion, in Port Hope just west of Cobourg.

pillars.title: Lifetime Aftercare and a Way Back In
pillars.body: Every graduate gets lifetime access to CCFA's weekly aftercare groups. Before you go home, your counsellor writes a relapse prevention plan with you and the team puts you in touch with psychiatrists, psychologists and addiction counsellors in your own area. If you finished a stay of 45 days or longer and things start to slide, you can come back for a free two-week relapse prevention program. Family members can keep up their own counselling after discharge, and alumni stay connected through the Roots of Recovery community.

pillars.title: Physicians, Nurses and Counsellors Under One Roof
pillars.body: Medical care is led by addictions physicians, among them Dr. Ron Phillipson and Dr. Leonard Bienenstock, and nurses are on site around the clock. Therapy comes from registered psychotherapists, a registered psychologist and certified addictions counsellors, with clinical manager Annette Maxwell overseeing the program. Former Toronto Maple Leafs player Jim McKenny works with clients as a recovery coach. Twelve-step meetings are offered but not required, and counsellors also draw on CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing and SMART Recovery.

overviewH2: Canadian Centre for Addictions - Center Overview
overview: The Canadian Centre for Addictions (CCFA) is a leading private rehab facility offering comprehensive treatment for individuals struggling with alcohol and drug addictions. Located in a serene environment, CCFA provides a personalized approach to recovery, focusing on holistic care that addresses both the physical and mental aspects of addiction. Their expert team of healthcare professionals delivers evidence-based therapies, residential treatment programs, and ongoing support to ensure long-term success. With a commitment to compassionate care, CCFA helps individuals reclaim their lives and achieve lasting sobriety.
serviceCaption: 10 services · as listed on the centre's website
afterOverview: Residential stays at CCFA run 30, 45, 60, 75 or 90 days, and the clinical team suggests a length after your intake assessment. Detox, if you need it, usually takes three to ten days and leads straight into counselling with the same team. Depression, anxiety and trauma are treated alongside the addiction rather than after it. Men and women sleep in separate rooms and have their own process groups, and family can visit on weekends.

location.heading: Canadian Centre for Addictions in Cobourg, Ontario
location.intro: The centre is at 420 Division Street in Cobourg, a lakeside town in Northumberland County on the north shore of Lake Ontario. It's about an hour and 15 minutes east of Toronto on Highway 401, roughly 45 minutes from Oshawa or Peterborough and about an hour and a half from Kingston, so families in the GTA, Durham Region and the Quinte area can make weekend visits without much planning.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Canadian Centre for Addictions cost?
faqs.a: Recovery.com lists an estimated $23,500 for a 30-day stay at the Cobourg centre. CCFA doesn't publish a price list on its own website and says the final cost depends on the program and how long you stay. Financing through Medicard is available, with terms from 6 months to 6 years and no down payment.

faqs.q: How long is treatment at CCFA?
faqs.a: Residential programs run 30, 45, 60, 75 or 90 days. The clinical team recommends a length after your intake assessment, based on how severe the addiction is and any mental health needs. If you need detox, it usually takes three to ten days at the start of your stay.

faqs.q: Does the Canadian Centre for Addictions provide medical detox on-site?
faqs.a: Yes, CCFA offers on-site medical detoxification, providing a safe and supervised environment to help individuals manage withdrawal symptoms under the care of medical professionals.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at Woodlawn Inn, 420 Division Street in Cobourg, Ontario, in Northumberland County. Most people drive in along Highway 401: it's about an hour and 15 minutes from Toronto and around an hour and a half from Kingston. Cobourg is also a stop on VIA Rail's Toronto to Montreal line.

faqs.q: Is CCFA private? Can I use insurance or work benefits?
faqs.a: Yes, CCFA is a private, fee-for-service centre and doesn't offer government-funded beds. The centre says many private health plans cover accredited residential treatment in full or in part, and it can provide paperwork to support a claim. Part of the cost may also qualify for the CRA medical expense tax credit, so it's worth asking your accountant.

faqs.q: What types of addiction does the Canadian Centre for Addictions treat?
faqs.a: CCFA treats a wide range of substance addictions, including alcohol, cocaine, opioids, prescription drugs, heroin, marijuana, and ecstasy. They also offer on-site detox services to support clients through the withdrawal process.

faqs.q: What treatment programs are available at the Canadian Centre for Addictions?
faqs.a: CCFA offers personalized treatment programs that include residential rehab, holistic therapies, one-on-one counseling, group therapy, and aftercare support to help individuals maintain long-term recovery.

faqs.q: Is family involvement part of the recovery process at CCFA?
faqs.a: Yes, CCFA encourages family involvement in the recovery process through family therapy sessions and support programs, understanding that addiction affects not just the individual but their loved ones as well.

faqs.q: How does CCFA ensure long-term recovery for clients?
faqs.a: CCFA supports long-term recovery by offering comprehensive aftercare services, including relapse prevention plans, ongoing counseling, and access to support groups, ensuring clients have the tools and support they need after leaving the facility.

faqs.q: What happens if I relapse after treatment?
faqs.a: Graduates of inpatient programs of 45 days or longer can come back for a free two-week relapse prevention program. Every graduate also keeps lifetime access to CCFA's weekly aftercare groups, so you're never starting from scratch.

faqs.q: Is the Canadian Centre for Addictions accredited?
faqs.a: Yes. CCFA has been accredited by Accreditation Canada since 2018 and is a member of the National Association of Addiction Treatment Providers (NAATP). It is also part of a research partnership with the University of Toronto studying recovery and cognition.
